verifierResult.exercise: Prediction checks compare expected versus modeled synthetic impact only.
verifierResult.negativeCase: A passing INTERRUPTED prediction leaves user impact interrupted.
verifierResult.invalidCase: Absent or invalid proof remains unknown, never successful continuity.

userImpactResult.syntheticSafeCase: r-before completes on v1 at 100 ms; distinct r-after admits to v2 at 60 ms and responds at 140 ms; original budgets, correct response and cart state preserved.
userImpactResult.syntheticPrematureRetirement: Old request interrupted at 70 ms; contradictory later response is not a completion.
userImpactResult.syntheticBudgetReset: 155 ms original elapsed exceeds 120 ms; reported 25 ms retry clock is ignored.
userImpactResult.syntheticUnknowns: Missing, forged, impossible or malformed evidence is explicitly unknown; attempted requests are not removed from counts.

iac.reason: Resource-free lesson; no cloud/IaC generation or deployment approval.

reviewer.status: Pending independent review of the published commit/tag

limits: A-S041 is one satisfier, not multiple credits for tests, cases or evidence.
No native Azure or actual HTTP assertion; all workload data and clocks are synthetic.
Correct old v1 completion is not a failed migration, nor proof a user moved.
A new v2 admission is request-level synthetic exposure, not durable user migration.
Read-only fixture does not establish write ordering, exactly-once effects or real host retry/drain behavior.
The conservative retirement gate covers only declared synthetic v1 work, not an actual service fleet.
Existing Node 22 test tooling does not approve any production runtime.
No package/global-runtime, cloud, IaC, credentials, shared-file or other-lesson changes.
B-S041 and original D-S041 native acceptance remain unfulfilled.
